description: NIST's Public Safety Communications extension for ns-3 models LTE device-to-device communication and mission-critical push-to-talk. It adds sidelink and relay behaviour, application traffic, building effects and reusable incident-scenario classes. Users define responders, movement, network configuration and applications; outputs include network traces, scenario descriptions and communication performance over simulated time. Coverage is globally configurable at local network scale, with no fixed observational dataset. Public C++ source is free under GPL-2.0, with NIST-authored portions in the United States public domain and GPL-2.0 terms abroad. A limitation is that legacy land-mobile radio is not supported and UE-to-network relay supports IPv6 only. The documented PSC 7.0 release follows ns-3.40; its large example has unresolved upstream assertion and trace-volume issues. The extension supports emergency-communications capacity and resilience studies on ns-3 (platform-ns-3). Official documentation cites the 2017 LTE D2D validation paper and 2021 MCPTT paper. No incident scenario was executed and no trace archive was downloaded.
